# Decision log

Short records of choices that shape the codebase. Newest first. Each one says what was decided, why, and what would make us revisit it.

## 2026-10-12 — Drizzle ORM instead of Prisma

**Decision:** use Drizzle ORM with `pg` and SQL migrations generated by `drizzle-kit`.

**Why:**
- Prisma needs a native engine binary downloaded at install time; that failed in a restricted build environment. Drizzle is plain TypeScript and needs no binary.
- Phase 2 needs a Postgres exclusion constraint (`EXCLUDE USING gist` on `tstzrange`) to make double bookings impossible. Drizzle's migrations are plain SQL files we can hand-edit, which suits this.
- Queries read like SQL, which makes transactions and row locks explicit.

**Revisit if:** the team strongly prefers Prisma's API and installs work everywhere it runs.

## 2026-10-12 — Postgres is the only source of truth

**Decision:** bookings live in Postgres. Google Calendar, if used, is a one-way mirror.

**Why:** two writable sources (calendar + DB) kept in sync by webhooks create race conditions and stale availability. One source plus a database constraint gives a guarantee instead of a best effort.

## 2026-10-12 — Node API owns every write; the Python agent never touches the DB

**Decision:** the voice agent calls narrow tool endpoints on the Node API with a service token.

**Why:** validation, policy checks, confirmation gating, idempotency and audit logging live in one place. The LLM interprets language; the backend owns truth.

## 2026-10-12 — Business routes are scoped by slug until auth arrives

**Decision:** Phase 0 routes are `/api/v1/businesses/:slug/...`. Phase 4 adds auth; dashboard routes will then take the business from the signed-in user, and the slug routes stay only for public, read-only data.
